releaseNotes: machine/ is finished. The four remaining files whose homes were arguable after v0.56.0 are placed by the same subject-of-the-assertion rule: audit-skill-links.ts (its own header: link-graph integrity for the shipped skill) and refresh-source-freshness.ts (maintains machine/source-registry.yaml) grade the skill, so they join machine/; validate-project-state.ts grades a business repo PROJECT_STATE and validate-state.ts grades a business design state, so they become gates/process/ and gates/design/. scripts/ now holds only renderers, probes, seeds, install-hooks, version, migrate-founder-gates, grade-screenshots, promote-design-tokens, run-audit.ts and lib/.

skill-version.json stays at the skill root, and this is now recorded in ARCHITECTURE.md rather than left implicit. It is the one file that must be readable by something that has not loaded the skill yet: SKILL.md tells an agent to compare it manually when check:skill-version is unavailable, which only works at a stable shallow path; and check:skill-version compares the manifest across --source and --installed, so burying it one level down would make that comparison depend on the installed copy having the same internal layout, which is exactly the drift a version check exists to detect. machine/ holds what a maintainer runs; skill-version.json is what the outside world reads.

The two parity fixtures that materialise a synthetic scripts/validate-project-state.ts were deliberately left alone. They build a fake skill root to exercise check-package-parity, and scripts/ is still one of the three roots findScriptPath searches, so the stub resolves correctly and the fixture proves the parser accepts any root rather than a hardcoded one.

check:gates-layout makes the layout self-defending instead of a convention someone has to remember. It reads the permitted domains from playbook/ rather than hardcoding them, so the two trees cannot drift; it fails a gate left at the gates/ root, because ARCHITECTURE.md deliberately has no top-level exception bucket; and it fails a basename held by two domains at once. That last rule restores a guarantee the layout gave up: a FLAT gates/ made duplicate basenames structurally impossible, since one directory cannot hold two files of the same name, and mirroring traded that away for browsability. Callers address scripts by basename alone, so a collision is not cosmetic — indexScripts already threw on it, but only at spawn time, which is a backstop rather than a gate.

Audit step count moves 70 to 71 and the fixture count 718 to 723. Four of the five new fixtures are failing-path cases, one per rule, each asserting the issue code rather than just exit 1 — an exit-code-only assertion passes when the validator crashes, which is a trap this repo has already been bitten by.

Review round: three shipped-guidance misses the move itself did not surface. playbook/design/design-room.md still listed scripts/validate-state.ts in its in-the-skill inventory, routing an agent to a file this change deletes — the v0.55.0 markdown sweep only covered check-*.ts basenames, so the validate-* moves were never swept by it. docs/VALIDATORS.md, which AGENTS.md designates the complete gate reference, was missing check:gates-layout, and its check:reference-size row still described a budget over references/, a directory that has not existed since v0.53.0. ARCHITECTURE.md also still carried the now-false paragraph saying these four validators were deliberately left in scripts/.
